input: Prepare me for a meeting with Gong (gong.io)

what_they_do.value: Gong harnesses the power of AI to transform how revenue teams win, unifying data, insights, and workflows into a single, trusted system that observes, guides, and acts alongside revenue teams.

priorities.priority: Move from revenue insight to agentic action through Gong Activate.
priorities.evidence: Gong announced Gong Activate as the next generation of Revenue AI, with always-on agents evaluating accounts, opportunities, and revenue plays and executing the motions that win, retain, and grow accounts from a shared blueprint.

priorities.priority: Expand and improve revenue data through sales enrichment.
priorities.evidence: Mission Callisto introduced Gong Enrich to fill missing account and contact details and expand the Gong Revenue Graph with third-party data, reducing the research burden on sellers.

priorities.priority: Automate repeatable revenue workflows with custom agents and deeper analysis.
priorities.evidence: Gong launched Agent Builder for custom event-triggered agents and Deep Mode in Gong Assistant for grounded investigation of hard business questions; it also described the Revenue Harness as an execution and governance layer for Custom Agents.

priorities.priority: Scale AI-native product development and R&D.
priorities.evidence: Gong appointed Liron Shtraichman as Chief R&D Officer, explicitly charging him with expanding Gong's agentic capabilities across the Revenue Graph, Revenue Harness, and Revenue Operating Surfaces.

priorities.priority: Make productivity and measurable revenue outcomes the operating focus.
priorities.evidence: At Celebrate '26, Gong described productivity as effectiveness multiplied by efficiency and highlighted its own reported reductions in seller ramp time, increased rep attainment, and productivity gains from connecting conversations, business signals, and revenue context.

challenges.challenge: Turning AI experimentation into trusted, scalable enterprise execution.
challenges.evidence: Gong said enterprises are no longer satisfied with evaluating AI and want scalable results, while nuanced revenue work requires deep contextual intelligence before it can be trusted; Gong Activate is positioned as its response.

challenges.challenge: Incomplete account and contact data is slowing sellers down.
challenges.evidence: Gong described data gaps as a source of seller friction and launched Gong Enrich to automatically fill missing account and contact details and reduce manual research.

challenges.challenge: Revenue teams are under pressure to grow, adopt AI, develop talent, and improve productivity while dealing with disconnected systems and incomplete information.
challenges.evidence: Gong's Celebrate recap explicitly described these pressures as the challenges facing revenue organizations and framed its event around helping teams create more revenue per rep.

challenges.challenge: Securing and governing AI agents as they take on more revenue-cycle work.
challenges.evidence: Gong appointed a CISO responsible for security, privacy, and compliance as agents take on more work, and emphasized scoped data access, audit trails, and configurable human oversight in its Revenue Harness.

recent_changes.headline: Gong appoints Liron Shtraichman as Chief R&D Officer and Guy Havusha as CISO
recent_changes.summary: The appointments strengthen engineering and security leadership as Gong accelerates agentic Revenue AI and expands enterprise security, privacy, and compliance programs.

recent_changes.headline: Gong named a Leader in the 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Revenue Action Orchestration
recent_changes.summary: Gong said it was one of four Leaders among 13 evaluated and was positioned highest for Ability to Execute and furthest for Completeness of Vision, for the second consecutive year.

recent_changes.headline: Gong launches Mission Callisto, Gong Activate, Gong Enrich, Agent Builder, and Deep Mode
recent_changes.summary: The launches broaden Gong from conversation intelligence toward a Revenue AI operating system that connects data, insights, workflows, and agents to execute revenue plays.

key_people.name: Amit Bendov
key_people.title: Co-founder and Chief Executive Officer
key_people.recent: At Celebrate '26, he positioned Gong's next phase as agentic AI that moves from telling teams how to win to helping win deals, and announced Gong Activate.

key_people.name: Liron Shtraichman
key_people.title: Chief R&D Officer
key_people.recent: Appointed on November 4, 2026, he said he would push Gong's agentic innovation further and is responsible for R&D across the Revenue Graph, Revenue Harness, and Revenue Operating Surfaces.

key_people.name: Guy Havusha
key_people.title: Chief Information Security Officer
key_people.recent: Appointed CISO on November 4, 2026, he took responsibility for global security, privacy, and compliance as Gong's AI agents act on customer data.

key_people.name: Shane Evans
key_people.title: Chief Revenue Architect
key_people.recent: At Celebrate '26, he made productivity—effectiveness multiplied by efficiency—the central revenue-operations priority and discussed Gong's own productivity transformation.

key_people.name: Simon Frey
key_people.title: Chief Customer Officer
key_people.recent: He hosted the Executive Showcase at Celebrate '26, bringing customer revenue leaders together to discuss operational hurdles and playbooks for using Revenue AI.

talking_points: Gong Activate and Agent Builder move from insight to action—where does Gong most need help scaling governed, reliable agent workflows across enterprise customers?
With Gong Enrich addressing account and contact-data gaps, which data-quality or enrichment bottlenecks still most constrain seller productivity?
As the new R&D and security leadership takes shape, how is Gong balancing faster AI-native product development with privacy, auditability, and human oversight?
